# Code review: SafeScope tx-flow parameterisation

**What was reviewed:** `9060a35...5636a0a`, committed changes only (from merge-base `913ee53` to HEAD). 34 files, +1412 / −67. Web app, TypeScript and React, Jest. Nothing was edited, no tests were run and nothing was posted.

## Summary

| | |
|---|---|
| **Verdict** | Fine to open the PR. Nothing blocks it. |
| **Why nothing blocks** | `SafeScopeProvider` isn't mounted anywhere in production yet (only in tests and Storybook), so every finding below is dormant today. |
| **What held it back** | The provider's `scope` object gets a new identity on every poll, and a stale "SDK not initialized" error sticks in `ConfirmProposedTx`. Both go live the moment a Space-level flow mounts the provider. |
| **Fix first** | F1 and F2. Each is a one-line change. |
| **Overall score** | About 76/100. This is my own estimate, not produced by the scoring stage. |

## Scores by area (worst first)

| Area | Score | Driven by |
|---|---|---|
| Bugs | 65 | F1, F2, F3 |
| Architecture | 75 | F4, F5 (contested), F6 (contested) |
| Testing | 80 | F7 |
| Regression | 95 | Unscoped paths keep their old behaviour. The new signature params are optional and appended last. |
| Security | 95 | No attacker-reachable path. The "fail closed" guard is a plus. |
| Performance | 90 | Folded into F1: a refetch every 15s. |
| DRY, KISS, conventions | 90 | Nothing worth filing. The `eslint-disable` for `exhaustive-deps` is explained, and the deep-import comments are justified. |

## What this review did not cover

- I ran the nine category passes myself rather than as nine parallel agents.
- The leave-it-better cleanup stage was skipped.
- The since-last-run file (`.git/safe-code-review`) was neither read nor written, to keep the run fully read-only.
- Adjudication covered 6 of 7 findings; F7 (tests) was not adjudicated.

## Findings

**F1 · P2 · Bugs · CONFIRMED** (both agents agreed it's real; they differed on likelihood)
`apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/safe-scope/SafeScopeProvider.tsx:139`
- **What:** `isFetching` is in the `scope` useMemo deps. It flips true then false on every 15s poll, so each poll produces two new `scope` objects even when no data changed. `safeLoading` stays stable in value, but the object identity doesn't.
- **Effect:** `ConfirmProposedTx.tsx:29` has `scope` in its effect deps. So it re-runs `createExistingTx` twice per poll: it refetches the tx details from the backend and replaces `safeTx` with a new object mid-review. `useSafeInfo` also returns a new object on every poll (`useSafeInfo.ts:17-37`). The `SafeTxProvider` effect re-runs too, but its nonce/safeTxGas check makes that harmless.
- **Fix:** compute `safeLoading` outside the memo and depend on it instead of `isFetching`. Also have `ConfirmProposedTx` depend on `scope?.sdk` rather than the whole `scope`.
- **Test:** the existing poll test at `SafeScopeProvider.test.tsx:275` only checks values. Add an identity check (`toBe`) across a poll.

**F2 · P2 · Bugs · CONFIRMED** (the validator found it partial, the refuter couldn't knock it down)
`apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/flows/ConfirmTx/ConfirmProposedTx.tsx:29`
- **What:** under a scope, `ConfirmProposedTx` runs on mount before `scope.sdk` has resolved. `getAndValidateSafeSDK(scope)` (`sdk.ts:37-42`) throws, and the error goes into `setSafeTxError`. When the SDK arrives, the effect runs again and `setSafeTx` succeeds, but nothing clears `safeTxError`. The only place that clears it is `SafeTxProvider.tsx:112`, in an unrelated effect.
- **Effect:** `ReviewTransactionContent.tsx:78` keeps showing a `TxCheckError` banner next to a valid transaction, and `logError(_103)` fires on every scoped mount.
- **Fix:** skip the call until `scope.sdk` is set, or call `setSafeTxError(undefined)` when it succeeds.

**F3 · P2 · Bugs · CONFIRMED** (both agents agreed it's real; they differed on likelihood)
`apps/web/src/services/tx/tx-sender/dispatch.ts:307`
- **What:** `dispatchTxExecution` receives `scope`, but still calls `getUserNonce(signerAddress)`, which reads the URL-chain `getWeb3ReadOnly()` (`hooks/wallets/web3.ts:58`). `txOptions.nonce` is only set when the user overrides the nonce manually.
- **Effect:** in a scoped flow on another chain, the stored `signerNonce` comes from the wrong chain. `SimpleTxWatcher` compares it with the scoped chain's live nonce to spot replacements. That can wrongly flag a successful tx as replaced (FAILED), or miss a real replacement. Speed-up also reuses this value (`SpeedUpModal:83`).
- **Fix:** pass `scope?.web3ReadOnly` into `getUserNonce`.

**F4 · P2 · Architecture · CONFIRMED** (both agents agreed it's real; they differed on likelihood)
`apps/web/src/services/contracts/safeContracts.ts:30` (also lines 64, 92, 157, and `sdk.ts:69`)
- **What:** the rule "never silently use the URL Safe" is only partly enforced.
  - `getGnosisSafeContract` still falls back to the unscoped `getSafeSDK()` to read the version. That path is reachable from the scoped `dispatchTxRelay` when `safe.version` is null.
  - `getReadOnlyMultiSendCallOnlyContract`, `getReadOnlySignMessageLibContract` and the proxy-factory and fallback-handler getters take no `scope`.
  - Unscoped `getSafeProvider()` has no `hasActiveScope()` guard.
- **Effect:** once batch execution, on-chain message signing, or relaying for a Safe with no reported version run under a scope, they would silently use the URL chain's SDK or provider.
- **Fix:** either add the same `hasActiveScope()` guard to `getSafeProvider`, `getGnosisSafeContract` and the contract getters, or thread `scope` through them. At minimum, document which flows are out of scope.

**F5 · P3 · Architecture · CONTESTED** (the validator confirmed it; the refuter argued it's intended and dormant)
`apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/safe-scope/activeScope.ts:8` and `apps/web/src/services/tx/tx-sender/sdk.ts:45`
- **What:** the guard is a process-wide counter, not tied to the React tree. While any provider is mounted, every unscoped `getAndValidateSafeSDK()` caller anywhere in the app throws. That includes the six scope-less `create*Tx` helpers in `create.ts`. Separately, `executionPreChecks.ts:137-142` catches that throw and silently skips the BAD_SIGNATURE check.
- **Refuter's case:** fail-closed is the intended design, and the pre-check being best-effort is documented.
- **Suggestion:** keep fail-closed, but don't let the pre-check swallow the "missing scope" error. Rethrow it and only skip on "not initialized".

**F6 · P3 · Architecture · CONTESTED** (the validator confirmed it; the refuter argued it's dormant)
`apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/safe-scope/context.ts:10` and `apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/safe-scope/SafeScopeProvider.tsx:123`
- **What:** a provider mounted with no target yet yields `scope === undefined`. That looks exactly like having no provider at all. So `useSafeInfo`, `useChainId`, `useSafeSDK` and `useWeb3ReadOnly` fall back to the URL Safe inside the flow until the user picks one.
- **Suggestion:** have `useSafeScope` tell "no provider" apart from "provider, nothing selected", for example with an `inScope` flag, so those hooks return empty values in the second case.

**F7 · P3 · Testing · not adjudicated**
`apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/safe-scope/__tests__/SafeScopeProvider.test.tsx:275`, `apps/web/src/components/tx-flow/flows/ConfirmTx/__tests__/ConfirmProposedTx.scope.test.tsx:17`, `apps/web/src/services/tx/executionPreChecks.ts:136`
- There's no test for `scope` identity staying stable across a poll (F1).
- There's no test for `ConfirmProposedTx` before the SDK is ready (F2).
- `executionPreChecks.test.ts` wasn't extended for the new `scope` param or the try/catch.

## Your call

| # | Suggested |
|---|---|
| F1, F2 | Fix now. They're cheap, and they sit on the exact path this PR exists for. |
| F3, F4 | Fix now, or file one ticket due before the provider is mounted in production. |
| F5, F6 | Discuss. They're design choices, and one agent argued each is intended. |
| F7 | Add the tests alongside the F1 and F2 fixes. |

## How this was produced

- The diff came from `git diff 9060a35...HEAD`. I reviewed it inline across all nine areas.
- For adjudication, 12 agents were planned (a validator and a refuter for each of 6 findings). F3/F4 and F5/F6 were each checked as a pair, so 8 agents ran.
- Results: F1–F4 were confirmed, with likelihood lowered because the provider isn't mounted in production yet. F5 and F6 were contested (confirmed by one agent, refuted by the other). Nothing was ruled out.
